Common.title: MiniSig
Common.description: A multisig wallet built from scratch, running on Base Sepolia. A teaching site that shows the mechanism.

HomePage.lead: A vault that will not move unless two keys agree, written in 140 lines of Solidity. The real thing is running on Base Sepolia.
HomePage.warning: Teaching material on a testnet. Do not store anything of value.

f1.title: One key is not enough
f1.desc: The contract holds the assets, not an address. It moves only when enough registered owners have signed.

f2.title: Keys never travel
f2.desc: Owners sign a hash of the transaction. The contract recovers the signer from the signature and checks it against the owner list.

f3.title: It rewrites itself
f3.desc: Adding an owner or changing the threshold also requires a resolution. There is no external administrator.

f4.title: API first
f4.desc: Everything the UI can do, the HTTP API can do. The server never holds a private key.

s1.title: Build a transaction
s1.desc: Enter a recipient and an amount; the contract itself returns the hash to sign.

s2.title: Collect signatures
s2.desc: Each owner signs in MetaMask. Nothing executes until the threshold is met.

s3.title: Execute
s3.desc: Submit with the collected signatures. The sender does not have to be an owner.

MiniSig.title: MiniSig
MiniSig.description: A hand-rolled multisig wallet on Base Sepolia (chain id 84532).
MiniSig.warning: This is teaching material. Do not store anything of value here. Use Safe in production.
MiniSig.txHashNote: txHash returned by the contract (this is what you sign)
MiniSig.collectNote: Collecting signatures happens off-chain. Here the API server stores them. Safe does the same thing with a dedicated service.
MiniSig.switchAccount: This key already signed — switch accounts in MetaMask
MiniSig.errNotOwnerSig: Signature is not from an owner
MiniSig.step1Help: Decide who receives how much from this vault. For testing, the quickest path is to pick one of the owners below. Nothing is sent yet — execution only becomes possible once the threshold of signatures is met.
MiniSig.warnSelf: The recipient is the contract itself. The vault would pay itself and the balance would not change (it still proves the mechanism works).
MiniSig.warnOverBalance: This exceeds the vault balance. Execution would fail.
MiniSig.warnBadAddress: Not a valid address (0x followed by 40 hex characters).
MiniSig.amountHint: A tiny amount is plenty on a testnet.

About.title: About this site
About.description: A teaching site that shows how a multisig works by running one.

what.title: What this is
what.body: A multisig wallet implemented from scratch rather than taken off the shelf, deployed to a real public chain (Base Sepolia), and operable from both a browser and an HTTP API. The contract is roughly 140 lines of Solidity with 17 tests.

why.title: Why build one
why.body: Clicking through an existing GUI teaches you very little. What does signing a transaction hash actually mean? Why is a nonce needed? Why does the same person signing twice not count as two people? Writing it yourself answers these. You should not, however, roll your own in production. The 2017 Parity incident froze roughly 514,000 ETH permanently through a multisig bug. If value is at stake, use Safe.

About.warning: This site only ever touches testnet assets. They have no real value.

Api.title: API
Api.description: Everything the UI can do, the HTTP API can do.
Api.intro: The boundary between operations that need a key and those that do not is exactly the boundary of this API. The server reads state, verifies and stores signatures, and assembles the transaction data. **Only signing and broadcasting happen client-side** — the server never holds a private key.
Api.e1: Current contract state (owners, threshold, nonce, balance)
Api.e3: Create a proposal. The txHash is computed by the contract, never accepted from the client
Api.e4: One proposal and the signatures collected so far
Api.e5: Add a signature. The signer is recovered and checked against the owner list; self-reported identity is ignored
Api.e6: If enough signatures exist, return ready-to-send calldata. **It does not broadcast**
Api.swaggerDesc: An interactive reference generated from the OpenAPI document. You can send requests straight from the browser.
Api.specNote: This API is described with OpenAPI 3.1.

twoHop.caption: A transfer takes two hops. You send an instruction; the contract pays out of its own balance. That is why your wallet shows value = 0.
twoHop.note: the ETH leaves from here, not from your balance

threshold.caption: The contract holds the assets, not an address. It moves only when enough owners have signed. One short, and nothing happens.

offChain.caption: The chain only ever sees the final call. How signatures are gathered is an off-chain problem — Safe runs a dedicated service for exactly this.
